entities.summary:
Cornelius Sabinus was a Roman senator and administrator active during the Late Republic era, playing a key role in the governance of the Roman provinces and serving under several prominent Roman leaders, including the dictator Sulla and the consul Gaius Marius. He was known for his diplomatic skills and military experience, which he leveraged to secure important positions and influence within the Roman government. Sabinus's legacy is marked by his efforts to promote the interests of the Roman people and maintain the stability of the Roman state, despite the tumultuous political climate of the Late Republic.

Sabinus's significance in the context of Roman history is underscored by his involvement in the governance of the Roman provinces, particularly in the eastern provinces, where he played a crucial role in maintaining Roman control and promoting Roman interests. His diplomatic and military expertise also made him a valuable asset to the Roman government, particularly during the tumultuous years of the Late Republic.

The impact of Sabinus's actions can be seen in the continued Roman dominance of the eastern provinces, as well as the preservation of Roman administrative structures and institutions. His legacy also serves as a reminder of the importance of effective governance and diplomacy in maintaining the stability of a great power.

Sabinus's life and career are marked by several striking statistics, including his extensive military service, which spanned over two decades, and his numerous diplomatic missions, which took him to various parts of the Roman world. He was also known for his extensive landholdings, which he acquired through his military victories and diplomatic efforts.

In the words of the Roman historian Plutarch, 'Cornelius Sabinus was a man of great intelligence and cunning, who was able to navigate the complex web of Roman politics with ease and emerge victorious.'
